column15: Standard range unpeated; rare peated casks exist in limited editions (e.g. Rare Cask Black) but are not the house style

Blended pot still + grain whiskey made at Midleton (Irish Distillers); malted barley is explicitly unpeated. Not parentSlug'd to a distillery row - treated as its own flagship line, same convention the brief uses for Johnnie Walker
Peated to ~35 ppm phenol, Port Ellen maltings
Peated to ~25-30 ppm phenol, mid-range on Islay

Standard single malt is unpeated. See rule.tsv for Peated (medium, ~23-24ppm) and Fusion (light, 25% peated Scottish malt); Kadhambam/Portonova/Raj Igala are cask-finish variants of the standard unpeated malt, no rule needed
Independent farm distillery, heavily peated floor-malted barley from Islay peat bogs

Renamed from "Rebel Yell" in 2020 (catalogue lists both names, both aliased here to one row); distilled at Lux Row Distillers, Bardstown KY. No source explicitly states unpeated - inferred from standard bourbon mashbill with no peated-malt mention

Canadian blended whisky, own distillery in Lethbridge AB; owned by Heaven Hill since 2019 (previously Constellation Brands). No explicit peat statement found; Canadian whisky has no peat tradition. defaultTypeName left empty - Canadian whisky has no clean match in the closed type list
Blend of 50% single malt / 50% single grain, produced by West Cork Distillers. No explicit peat statement; inferred unpeated from Irish tradition and absence of smoke in tasting notes

Oaxacan corn whiskey (85% corn / 15% malted barley), own distillery near Oaxaca city. No peat/smoke mentioned anywhere; defaultTypeName left empty - corn whiskey has no clean match in the closed type list
Made at Powerscourt Distillery, Co. Wicklow; range is 75% malt whiskey / 25% Irish pot still so defaultTypeName left empty. No explicit peat statement; inferred unpeated from Irish tradition
Bruichladdich's heavily peated brand, ~40ppm

Added because Port Charlotte (this batch) references it via parentSlug. Core Bruichladdich-branded range is unpeated; siblings Port Charlotte (heavy) and Octomore (extreme, not in this batch) are separate producer rows

Runs both peated (~45ppm, about a quarter of the year) and unpeated (~three quarters) malt, and often vats both together in one release; no reliable per-bottling signal from names alone ("On The Way", "Paris Edition", "Red Wine Cask"), so left unknown rather than guessed
Base "Malt Rye" (100% Finnish rye malt) is unpeated; sold as a distinct product line from the "Peat Smoke" and "Wood Smoke" variants, see rule.tsv

Blend of 15 malt and grain whiskies; no explicit peat statement, inferred unpeated from "delicate sweet, smooth mellow" tasting description with no smoke mentioned. Owner commonly associated with Whyte & Mackay in trade chatter but not confirmed via a source actually opened, left empty
The Kurayoshi pure/vatted malt, blended from malt whiskies sourced from various Scottish distilleries plus Japanese malt; no peat information found for the sourced components, left unknown
Could not find a reliable source for this exact brand (searches surfaced an unrelated "Restless Spirits" company); kind/country are guesses from naming convention only

Private-label range (bottled by First Blending Co / SVS La Martiniquaise) spanning at least Speyside and Highland single malt bottlings under one name; base/default peat level unclear so left unknown - see rule.tsv for the explicit "Peated" bottling
Blend of 80% single grain / 20% single malt, Co. Cork. No explicit peat statement; inferred unpeated from Irish tradition and tasting notes (honey, vanilla, toasted oak) with no smoke mentioned
No web presence found; own-label, product name itself says "Blend"
Kentucky Straight Bourbon, La Martiniquaise portfolio (sourced, not own distillery). No explicit peat statement; inferred unpeated - standard bourbon mashbill, no peated malt mentioned
Blended malt from 14 Highland and Islay whiskies; American Oak expression explicitly described as having "a touch of peat" / "hints of smoke" - a trace, not a peated whisky
The whisky is unpeated ... malted barley used is entirely unpeated (direct quote). Built for the J&B blend; own-name bottlings are the Flora & Fauna 10 Year Old

No search performed (small craft producer, 2 products); known from general knowledge as a Virginia craft rye distillery (Roundstone Rye), but no citation opened so peat left unknown rather than asserted
No web presence found; own-label, "Glen" naming convention suggests Scotch but unconfirmed
No web presence found; own-label, origin unclear

Svensk Rök ("Swedish Smoke", ~70% peated malt) is explicitly Mackmyra's first/only dedicated smoky release, implying the core range (incl. this batch's Björksav and Moment Tolv) is unpeated; no direct statement for those two specific bottlings, confidence kept low. See rule.tsv for Svensk Rök, added defensively though not itself in this batch's samples

Named for the historic Glasgow tall ship, NOT related to Glenlivet - verified as a distinct brand. 40% malt/60% grain blend by Aceo Spirits (parent of independent bottler Murray McDavid). No explicit peat statement; inferred unpeated from tasting notes (malty, honeyed, spiced oak, orange zest, vanilla, toffee) with no smoke mentioned

Verified distinct from Yamazaki - made at Asaka Distillery by Sasanokawa Shuzo. Malt + grain blend. No explicit peat statement; inferred unpeated from tasting notes (orchard fruit, salted caramel, vanilla) with no smoke mentioned

A lime-infused, sweetened Scotch-based "spirit drink" (35% ABV, sugar + vanilla extract added) rather than a standard whisky - FLAG FOR HUMAN REVIEW of categorisation. Base Ballantine's blend is generally light/touch-of-smoke, but given the heavy flavouring/dilution here peat character is uncertain, left unknown rather than inherited

Moldovan single malt (3-year, "Original Scottish Technology" claim) plus flavoured Honey/Apple variants, so defaultTypeName left empty. No smoke/peat mentioned in the thin, partly foreign-language sourcing available

No brand-specific source found; "Irish Blend" per catalogue sample name. peatProfile=none is a category-level inference (unpeated is the entrenched default style of Irish whiskey per the cited source), not a brand-specific confirmation - flagged for review

Single pot still Irish whiskey made at Midleton exclusively for Dublin merchant Mitchell & Son. No explicit "unpeated" statement for this specific bottling; inferred from Irish pot-still tradition, kept low confidence

Added because Green Spot (this batch) references it via parentSlug. Home of Jameson, Redbreast, Powers, Green Spot, Midleton Very Rare; malted barley used there is explicitly unpeated. defaultTypeName left empty - produces blend, single pot still and single malt

First Georgian whisky, Kartveli Distillery (founder Jimsher Chkhaidze). "Tsinandali" in the catalogue sample name is a wine-cask finish (aged in ex-Tsinandali-wine barrels), not a separate product or a wine product - this is genuinely a whisky. No peat/smoke mentioned; matured in Georgian wine and brandy casks. defaultTypeName left empty - only one expression researched, described as "blended" but full range unconfirmed
French whisky from the Gers/Gascony region, barley malt. No smoke/peat mentioned in tasting notes (vanilla, dried fruit, almonds, hazelnuts, caramel, apricot)
No web presence found for this exact brand; American whiskey/moonshine style assumed from name only

Van Winkle family's wheated-bourbon brand, distilled/bottled by Sazerac at Buffalo Trace under a joint venture since 2002. No explicit peat statement found (sources covered ownership/history, not tasting notes); inferred unpeated from standard bourbon mashbill

Added because Old Rip Van Winkle (this batch) references it via parentSlug. Produces both bourbon and rye so defaultTypeName left empty. No explicit peat statement found; inferred unpeated, standard American whiskey distillery

Blend of triple-distilled malt and grain whiskey, founded by Conor McGregor (Eire Born Spirits), now majority-owned by Proximo Spirits. No explicit peat statement; inferred unpeated from Irish tradition and tasting notes (vanilla, honey, toasted wood) with no smoke mentioned

Catalogue brand string for this row is "Seagram's Gin" but the sample product is "Seagram's Royal Stag Deluxe" - an Indian whisky (blend of grain spirits + imported Scotch malts), not a gin; almost certainly a shop miscategorisation. Row created for the actual (whisky) product; exact "Seagram's Gin" catalogue string aliased here - FLAG FOR HUMAN REVIEW. No explicit peat statement; inferred unpeated
Core range unpeated; "Savu" ("smoke") is their distinct peated single malt (~5ppm, light) - see rule.tsv, not itself in this batch's samples
Made at James Sedgwick Distillery, Wellington. Range spans blended and single malt so defaultTypeName left empty. No peat/smoke statement found in any source opened, left unknown rather than assumed
